messages:
Noah (People Ops): Heads-up: we've rolled out an 'Urgent Travel Return' addendum to PTO policy. Quick summary: limited reimbursement for emergency rebooking, expedited PTO advance (up to 3 days), and a lightweight manager checklist. Full doc + form: https://intranet.redwood/people/urgent-travel-return

Sam (Eng): When does this start? We had a teammate stuck in transit last week.

Noah (People Ops): Effective immediately. Pilot for 4 months; we'll collect anonymized usage metrics.

Zara (Travel): Reimbursement details: up to $450 per incident for unavoidable costs (rebook fee, one night hotel). No upgrades. Upload receipts to travel-expenses@redwood with subject URGENT-TRAVEL.

Ethan (Payroll): Advance pay: managers can authorize up to 3 days. Repayment options: spread across next 2 pay periods or a single deduction. Note: some countries require written consent for deductions.

Maya (Legal): Confirmed. Doc includes region list and consent template. Also added data retention guidance for receipts.

Sam (Eng): If the person is on an active incident rotation, should managers deny?

Noah (People Ops): Safety and leave law first. If denying risks the employee or breaks law, approve and follow staffing fallback: 1) post to rota channel, 2) request backup/oncall, 3) open temp coverage with staffing-ops. Checklist is in the doc.

rota-bot: Reminder: approved PTO affecting rota must be entered 24h before shift start or notify eng-oncall for manual swap.

Noah (People Ops): We'll hold a 20-min manager drop-in tomorrow 9am PT to walk through examples. Ping me or Zara for edge cases. Thanks! :wave:
